newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico, Panama agree to sign trade pact next year.
newsitem.headline: Mexico, Panama agree to sign trade pact next year.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo on Tuesday said he and his Panamanian counterpart had agreed to sign a free trade treaty before April 1998.
Panama and Mexico have been discussing the treaty since Zedillo visited the Central American nation in 1996.

"Both presidents have agreed that a good date by which to conclude these negotiations would be precisely before the continental meeting in Santiago, Chile, in April 1998," he said. An annual meeting of Latin American presidents is scheduled in Chile early next year.

After private talks with Panamanian President Ernesto Perez Balladares, Zedillo said both heads of state wanted to make what he called an extraordinary effort to intensify negotiations, starting probably in October.
Perez Balladares said the agreement would broaden and strengthen commercial ties between the two countries.
Trade between Mexico and Panama totaled $100.6 million in the first five months of this year, with an $84.6 million surplus on the Mexican side.
Perez Balladares also said he was interested in opening a international center in Panama to help combat the Latin American drug trade.
